prompt: Read `stdin` line by line into `commands`: each line stripped, skipping blank lines and comment lines starting with '#' (even indented ones).
given:
import io
stdin = io.StringIO("list

  load phi3  
# a comment
exit")
answer:
stripped = (line.strip() for line in stdin)
commands = [s for s in stripped if s and not s.startswith("#")]
check:
assert commands == ["list", "load phi3", "exit"], commands
rerun(stdin=io.StringIO("  # indented comment
   
run x
"))
assert commands == ["run x"], f"{commands}: strip BEFORE checking startswith('#')"
why: Iterating a stream yields lines with their '\n'; strip first, then test for blank and '#'.

prompt: Print each key/value of `pairs` to `out` as a 'key: value' line, using print's sep= and file=.
answer:
for key, value in pairs.items():
    print(key, value, sep=": ", file=out)
why: print(a, b, sep=': ', file=stream) writes to any text stream and converts non-strings for you.

prompt: On ONE line of `out`, write `label`, then one '.' per step (flushing after each dot), then ' done' and a newline.
given:
label, steps = "loading", 3
out = FlushCountingIO()   # a StringIO that counts flush() calls
answer:
print(label, end="", file=out)
for _ in range(steps):
    print(".", end="", file=out, flush=True)
print(" done", file=out)
check:
assert out.getvalue() == "loading... done\n", repr(out.getvalue())
assert out.flushes >= steps, f"{out.flushes} flushes: pass flush=True so a real terminal shows each dot now"
why: end='' suppresses the newline; flush=True pushes partial output to a terminal immediately.

prompt: Read `stdin` with readline() until EOF or an 'exit'/'quit' line (any case), appending each non-blank stripped line to `echoed`. A blank line must NOT end the loop.
given:
import io
stdin = io.StringIO("hi

  there 
EXIT
never
")
echoed = []
check:
assert echoed == ["hi", "there"], f"{echoed}: a blank line is '\\n' (truthy); only '' means EOF, so strip AFTER the EOF check"
assert stdin.read() == "never\n", "should stop reading at EXIT"
rerun(stdin=io.StringIO("hi"), echoed=[])
assert echoed == ["hi"], echoed
why: readline() returns '' only at EOF and '\n' for a blank line; test for EOF before stripping.

prompt: Write `main(argv, out, err) -> int` for `greet NAME...`: '--help' prints USAGE to out and returns 0; no names prints USAGE to err and returns 2; otherwise prints 'Hello, <names joined by spaces>.' to out and returns 0.
why: Asked-for help is success (stdout, 0); a usage error goes to stderr with exit 2. Run it as sys.exit(main(sys.argv[1:])).

prompt: Set `line` to e.g. '2026-09-14 10:03:22 ERROR model not loaded' (timestamp from `when`, level uppercased) and APPEND it plus a newline to `path`, creating missing parent folders. Running it twice must keep both lines.
given:
from datetime import datetime
path = tmp / "logs" / "deep" / "olm.log"   # tmp is a fresh temp dir; logs/deep doesn't exist yet
when, level, message = datetime(2026, 9, 14, 10, 3, 22), "error", "model not loaded"
setup:
import atexit, shutil, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
atexit.register(shutil.rmtree, tmp, True)
answer:
line = f"{when.strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')} {level.upper()} {message}"
path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
with open(path, "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(line + "\n")
check:
assert line == "2026-09-14 10:03:22 ERROR model not loaded", line
rerun(when=datetime(2026, 9, 14, 10, 3, 25), level="INFO", message="loaded phi3")
text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
assert text == "2026-09-14 10:03:22 ERROR model not loaded\n2026-09-14 10:03:25 INFO loaded phi3\n", f"{text!r}: 'w' truncates, 'a' appends; write() adds no newline"
why: open(p, 'a') appends ('w' truncates); mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True) is safe to repeat.

prompt: Build an argparse parser (prog 'weather'): positional `city` of 1+ words, `--days` int default 1, `--unit` C or F default F, `-v/--verbose` flag. Parse `argv` into `args`; on bad input set `args = None` instead of exiting.
answer:
p = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="weather")
p.add_argument("city", nargs="+")
p.add_argument("--days", type=int, default=1)
p.add_argument("--unit", choices=["C", "F"], default="F")
p.add_argument("-v", "--verbose", action="store_true")
try:
    args = p.parse_args(argv)
except SystemExit:
    args = None
check:
assert args is not None and vars(args) == {"city": ["New", "York"], "days": 3, "unit": "C", "verbose": False}, f"{args} (did you pass argv to parse_args?)"
rerun(argv=["-v", "Durham"])
assert args is not None and vars(args) == {"city": ["Durham"], "days": 1, "unit": "F", "verbose": True}, args
rerun(argv=["Durham", "--unit", "K"])
assert args is None, "bad input: argparse raises SystemExit(2); catch it and set args = None"
rerun(argv=[])
assert args is None, "city is required"
why: parse_args(argv) (not the default sys.argv); bad input raises SystemExit, so catch it in a REPL or test.

prompt: Write each `notes` entry to root/notes/<name>.md as UTF-8 (create folders as needed), then set `stems` to the sorted file stems of all .md files in that folder.
given:
root = tmp / "vault"   # root/notes/ already holds old.md and readme.txt
notes = {"b": "beta", "a": "älpha"}
setup:
import atexit, shutil, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
atexit.register(shutil.rmtree, tmp, True)

(tmp / "vault" / "notes").mkdir(parents=True)
(tmp / "vault" / "notes" / "old.md").write_text("x", encoding="utf-8")
(tmp / "vault" / "notes" / "readme.txt").write_text("x", encoding="utf-8")
answer:
folder = root / "notes"
folder.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
for name, text in notes.items():
    (folder / f"{name}.md").write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
stems = sorted(p.stem for p in folder.glob("*.md"))
check:
assert stems == ["a", "b", "old"], stems
assert (root / "notes" / "a.md").read_bytes() == "älpha".encode("utf-8"), "pass encoding='utf-8' to write_text (Windows defaults to cp1252)"
rerun(root=tmp / "x" / "y", notes={"n": "1"})
assert stems == ["n"], f"{stems}: create missing parent folders too"
why: Path / 'x' joins, write_text(..., encoding='utf-8'), glob order isn't guaranteed so sort, .stem drops the suffix.

prompt: Set `data` to a copy of `defaults` overlaid with the JSON object in `path` (missing file or invalid JSON: just the defaults; never mutate `defaults`), then save `data` back to `path` with json.dump.
setup:
import atexit, shutil, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
atexit.register(shutil.rmtree, tmp, True)
answer:
data = dict(defaults)
try:
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as f:
        data.update(json.load(f))
except (FileNotFoundError, json.JSONDecodeError):
    pass
with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    json.dump(data, f, indent=2)
check:
assert data == {"unit": "F", "days": 1}, data
assert json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) == data, "save data back to path with json.dump(data, f)"
path.write_text('{"unit": "C"}', encoding="utf-8")
rerun()
assert data == {"unit": "C", "days": 1}, data
assert defaults == {"unit": "F", "days": 1}, f"defaults mutated to {defaults}; copy it with dict(defaults)"
path.write_text("{not json", encoding="utf-8")
rerun()
assert data == {"unit": "F", "days": 1}, f"{data}: invalid JSON should fall back to defaults"
why: json.load(f)/json.dump(obj, f) take files (loads/dumps take strings); bad JSON raises json.JSONDecodeError.

prompt: Read `src` into `rows` (a list of dicts) with csv.DictReader and set `total` to the sum of its tokens column; then write the rows sorted by model to `dst` with csv.DictWriter (columns model, ms, tokens; header first).
given:
import csv
src, dst = tmp / "runs.csv", tmp / "sorted.csv"   # src has a header row: model,ms,tokens
setup:
import atexit, shutil, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
atexit.register(shutil.rmtree, tmp, True)

(tmp / "runs.csv").write_text("model,ms,tokens\nphi3,120,40\nllama3,900,50\nphi3,130,30\n", encoding="utf-8")
answer:
with open(src, newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    rows = list(csv.DictReader(f))
total = sum(int(r["tokens"]) for r in rows)
with open(dst, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    w = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=["model", "ms", "tokens"])
    w.writeheader()
    w.writerows(sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r["model"]))
check:
assert total == 120, f"{total!r}: csv values are all strings; int() them"
raw = dst.read_bytes()
assert b"\r\r\n" not in raw, "blank lines between rows: open the output with newline=''"
assert raw.decode("utf-8").splitlines() == ["model,ms,tokens", "llama3,900,50", "phi3,120,40", "phi3,130,30"], raw
why: Open csv files with newline='' (else Windows writes \r\r\n); DictReader values are always str.

prompt: Set `widths` to each column's max length over the header and all cells, then `lines` to the header and each row formatted per column with its align char and width, joined by two spaces, trailing spaces stripped.
answer:
widths = [max(len(x) for x in col) for col in zip(headers, *rows)]
fmt = lambda vals: "  ".join(f"{v:{a}{w}}" for v, a, w in zip(vals, align, widths)).rstrip()
lines = [fmt(headers)] + [fmt(r) for r in rows]
check:
assert widths == [10, 4, 6], widths
assert lines == ["model       size  family", "phi3:mini    2.3  phi", "llama3:70b  39.0  llama"], f"{lines} (trailing spaces? rstrip() each line)"
rerun(headers=["name", "n"], rows=[["a", "1"], ["bb", "22"]], align="<<")
assert lines == ["name  n", "a     1", "bb    22"], f"{lines}: rstrip() the trailing padding"
why: zip(headers, *rows) transposes rows into columns; a nested spec f'{v:{a}{w}}' interpolates align and width.

prompt: Create `parser = RaisingParser(prog='olm')` with REQUIRED subcommands whose name lands in args.cmd: `list` (no args) and `run MODEL PROMPT...` (prompt is 1+ words). Parse `argv` into `args`.
given:
import argparse
class RaisingParser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    def error(self, message):       # raise instead of printing + SystemExit
        raise ValueError(message)
argv = ["run", "phi3", "tell", "me", "a", "joke"]
answer:
parser = RaisingParser(prog="olm")
sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
sub.add_parser("list")
run = sub.add_parser("run")
run.add_argument("model")
run.add_argument("prompt", nargs="+")
args = parser.parse_args(argv)
why: add_subparsers(dest='cmd', required=True): without dest you can't tell which ran; without required [] parses fine.

prompt: Write `main(argv) -> int` for `todo done N`: return 2 if parser.parse_args raises ValueError; load the todo list from JSON `path`; return 1 if N isn't in 1..len; otherwise set that todo's 'done' to True, save the list back to `path`, return 0.
given:
import json
# parser (defined for you): a RaisingParser with one subcommand `done N` (N: int);
# parser.parse_args(argv) raises ValueError on bad usage.
path = tmp / "todos.json"   # [{"text": "buy milk", "done": false}, {"text": "call mom", "done": false}]
setup:
import atexit, shutil, tempfile
from pathlib import Path
tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
atexit.register(shutil.rmtree, tmp, True)

import argparse, json
class RaisingParser(argparse.ArgumentParser):
    def error(self, message):
        raise ValueError(message)
parser = RaisingParser(prog="todo")
parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True).add_parser("done").add_argument("n", type=int)
(tmp / "todos.json").write_text(json.dumps([{"text": "buy milk", "done": False}, {"text": "call mom", "done": False}]), encoding="utf-8")
check:
assert main(["done", "2"]) == 0
saved = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
assert saved == [{"text": "buy milk", "done": False}, {"text": "call mom", "done": True}], saved
assert main(["done", "9"]) == 1, "out of range is a runtime failure: exit 1"
assert main(["done", "0"]) == 1, "0 is out of range too (todos[-1] is the LAST todo)"
assert main(["done", "two"]) == 2, "bad usage: exit 2"
assert main([]) == 2, "missing subcommand: exit 2"
assert json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) == saved, "failed commands must not change the file"
why: Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 runtime failure, 2 usage error; validate 1 <= n <= len before indexing (n=0 hits todos[-1]).
